jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**Company Overview**
--------------------

Verne is building physical AI to make physical work as scalable as software and bring general-purpose robots to every business. We develop robots, foundation models, and the tools that turn them into reliable industrial deployments.

Our open-weight world action model, Verne V0.5, brings together video and action learning. Alongside it, we build data and training systems, a fine-tuning platform, and inference and control software. Our work is grounded in real deployments: learning new tasks efficiently, adapting to different environments, and operating reliably in production.

**The Role**
------------

We’re looking for a talented Software Engineer to design and build the core systems that power Verne’s robots in the real world. This is a hands-on role where your work will directly translate to physical robots performing customer-critical tasks. You’ll work across the full robotics software stack, from low-level sensor and actuator interfaces, to deploying large-scale policy learning pipelines, to shipping reliable features that customers depend on. Beyond just writing code, you’ll help design solutions, lead engineering efforts, and think cross-functionally to bridge hardware, machine learning, and product requirements.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* Build and optimize robotics software in Python and C++, spanning device drivers, control interfaces, and high-level APIs that power real-world deployments.
* Integrate and deploy ML policies (PyTorch) into visuomotor control loops, ensuring efficient inference on edge hardware.
* Design and test training pipelines for policy learning, including dataset preparation, augmentation, and scaling across massive multi-modal datasets (video, teleop trajectories, sensor streams).
* Develop infrastructure for teleoperation and autonomy, including real-time data streaming, low-latency WebRTC systems, and fallback human-in-the-loop control.
* Prototype new robot capabilities by collaborating closely with the hardware and research teams, translating experimental ideas into production-ready features.
* Systematically evaluate and test policies through lab trials and live customer proofs of concept, measuring performance, robustness, and safety at scale.
* Contribute to cloud + edge scaling efforts, including AWS-based data ingestion pipelines, IoT fleet management, and distributed training/serving infrastructure.
* Take ownership of engineering projects end-to-end, from design discussions and architecture, to implementation, testing, and deployment in the field.
* Work cross-functionally with product, research, and customer teams to ensure the systems you build align with real-world needs and unlock tangible customer value.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* B.S., M.S., Ph.D. in computer science or related fields.
* Strong programming skills in Python (you write clean, efficient, production-ready code)
* Solid experience with PyTorch and modern ML workflows
* Systems engineering skills (networking, concurrency, performance)
* At least 3 years of full-time work experience for candidates with a B.S. in related fields. 1 year of experience for M.S. or Ph.D. candidates.
* Experience with robotic arms, embedded systems, etc (e.g., Arduinos, motors, robot arms)

**Preferred**
-------------

* Experience with real-time systems (cameras, sensors, streaming)
* Hands-on with AWS services (EC2, IoT, WebRTC)

**Why Join Us**
---------------

At Verne, you won’t just be writing code, you’ll be shaping the future of physical AI. You’ll see your work run on real robots, in real customer environments, with immediate impact. You’ll join a small, world-class team where your contributions matter and your growth is accelerated.

**Details**
-----------

* Location: South San Francisco, CA (on-site required)
* Compensation: Competitive salary + meaningful equity
* Perks: Free meals vouchers, hardware access, health benefits, PTO

This is a rare chance to join a YC-backed robotics startup early and help build the foundation of the company. If you’re excited about robots, passionate about solving hard problems, and eager to see your work come alive in the real world — we’d love to hear from you.

Compensation Range: $140K - $200K

jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**Your best work shouldn't be hidden behind your last employer's name.**  
  
Some of the strongest engineers we've worked with wouldn't stand out in a résumé stack. They didn't all come from FAANG. They didn't all have CS degrees from the usual schools. Some did, some didn't, and it made less difference than you'd think.

What made them stand out: hand them an ambiguous problem and an unfamiliar codebase, and they shipped something real. Quickly.

They read the code before asking for help. They picked up new tools without being told to. They weren't thrown by systems they didn't understand on day one. And they built things that held up in production.  
  
**That's who we're looking for.**  
  
**The opportunity**

Peri is recruiting Software Engineers, including founding and early backend roles, for some of New York's most compelling AI startups, from Seed to Series D+, backed by investors including a16z, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, Notable Capital, and Thrive.

We've worked closely with the founders, studied the engineers who thrive on their teams, and learned what really sets them apart.

The short version: **Ownership, speed, technical judgment, and the ability to learn fast often count for more than the name at the top of your last offer letter.**

You don't need to have worked on AI products already. If you have, great. If you haven't, keep reading.  
  
**What you'll actually do**

Imagine joining a team where the product is still taking shape.

There's no thick onboarding doc. The architecture has decisions you'd make differently. The roadmap changes when a customer says something surprising.

Your job is to make it work. Understand what users actually need. Make the tradeoffs. Design the system, write the code, ship it, and fix it when real traffic finds what tests didn't.

You're part builder, part architect, part problem-solver.

You'll work directly with founders. You'll own features and systems end to end, not just tickets. And you'll see your work in front of customers within days, not quarters.

These roles are for engineers who like having the whole problem.  
  
**Who we're looking for**

Maybe you're an engineer at a big company who keeps wanting to touch more of the stack than your team allows.

Maybe you taught yourself, switched careers, or grew into responsibilities long before anyone gave you the title for them.

**We take all of that seriously.**

But here's the thing.

**We need you to show us.**

A résumé won't tell us how you debug something you've never seen, how you make decisions with incomplete information, or what you do when the obvious approach falls over.

So walk us through it.

Tell us about a system you designed. A bug that took you days to track down. A technology you had to master in a week. Something you built that nobody asked you to build.

It doesn't need to be impressive-sounding. It needs to be real.  
  
**Why aren't the companies listed?**

Because this isn't one opening.

We work with several teams looking for similar engineers, each building something different.

Rather than you running six interview loops in parallel, we'd like to understand how you think and what you're great at, then point you toward the teams where you'd fit best.

We only work with companies we'd be excited to join ourselves.  
  
**Who is Peri?**

Most technical recruiting is keyword matching: languages, frameworks, years of experience, last employer.

We think that leaves a lot of great engineers on the table.

So we start from the other end. We learn from founders what actually makes an engineer succeed on their team, then look for those qualities in people whose résumés may undersell them.

We're most interested in engineers who are better than their credentials suggest.  
  
**How to apply**

* Apply here or DM me on LinkedIn.
* We do want one answer: **What's the hardest or most interesting thing you've built, and what about it makes you think you're capable of more than your résumé shows?**

  + A few sentences is enough. A link to code or a project is even better. Specifics beat buzzwords.
  + If there's a fit, we'll talk, share what we know about each team, and help you figure out which roles make sense. When there's a strong match, we'll connect you directly with the founders.

**And if you've ever thought, "I'm a much better engineer than my résumé makes me look," we especially want to hear from you.**  
  
**One last thing**

Looking past credentials doesn't mean looking past ability.

If you're mass-applying without reading the post, can't show real engineering work, have a fabricated or misleading LinkedIn profile, or aren't authorized to work in the United States, please don't apply.

**It's not a good use of anyone's time.**

We'll overlook a pedigree. We won't overlook a lack of effort, skill, or honesty.  
  
**Show us what you've shipped, not what you say you can ship.**

Compensation Range: $150K - $350K

Engineers today are building some of the most ambitious machines humanity has ever seen. They should have AI that’s purpose-built for them.

Hardware engineering teams use Nominal to simulate, test, manufacture, and operate the physical systems that keep the world moving, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation energy systems and robotics.

  
  

Our customers span aerospace, defense, manufacturing, transportation, energy, and robotics. ### **About Hardware Intelligence**

  
  

We're going after the biggest opportunities to accelerate how the world engineers: agents that are expert at engineering physical systems, not just competent at calling tools. new_jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer
new_jobs.description:
**Your best work shouldn't be hidden behind your last employer's name.**  
  
Some of the strongest engineers we've worked with wouldn't stand out in a résumé stack. They didn't all come from FAANG. They didn't all have CS degrees from the usual schools. Some did, some didn't, and it made less difference than you'd think.

What made them stand out: hand them an ambiguous problem and an unfamiliar codebase, and they shipped something real. Quickly.

They read the code before asking for help. They picked up new tools without being told to. They weren't thrown by systems they didn't understand on day one. And they built things that held up in production.  
  
**That's who we're looking for.**  
  
**The opportunity**

Peri is recruiting Software Engineers, including founding and early backend roles, for some of New York's most compelling AI startups, from Seed to Series D+, backed by investors including a16z, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, Notable Capital, and Thrive.

We've worked closely with the founders, studied the engineers who thrive on their teams, and learned what really sets them apart.

The short version: **Ownership, speed, technical judgment, and the ability to learn fast often count for more than the name at the top of your last offer letter.**

You don't need to have worked on AI products already. If you have, great. If you haven't, keep reading.  
  
**What you'll actually do**

Imagine joining a team where the product is still taking shape.

There's no thick onboarding doc. The architecture has decisions you'd make differently. The roadmap changes when a customer says something surprising.

Your job is to make it work. Understand what users actually need. Make the tradeoffs. Design the system, write the code, ship it, and fix it when real traffic finds what tests didn't.

You're part builder, part architect, part problem-solver.

You'll work directly with founders. You'll own features and systems end to end, not just tickets. And you'll see your work in front of customers within days, not quarters.

These roles are for engineers who like having the whole problem.  
  
**Who we're looking for**

Maybe you're an engineer at a big company who keeps wanting to touch more of the stack than your team allows.

Maybe you taught yourself, switched careers, or grew into responsibilities long before anyone gave you the title for them.

**We take all of that seriously.**

But here's the thing.

**We need you to show us.**

A résumé won't tell us how you debug something you've never seen, how you make decisions with incomplete information, or what you do when the obvious approach falls over.

So walk us through it.

Tell us about a system you designed. A bug that took you days to track down. A technology you had to master in a week. Something you built that nobody asked you to build.

It doesn't need to be impressive-sounding. It needs to be real.  
  
**Why aren't the companies listed?**

Because this isn't one opening.

We work with several teams looking for similar engineers, each building something different.

Rather than you running six interview loops in parallel, we'd like to understand how you think and what you're great at, then point you toward the teams where you'd fit best.

We only work with companies we'd be excited to join ourselves.  
  
**Who is Peri?**

Most technical recruiting is keyword matching: languages, frameworks, years of experience, last employer.

We think that leaves a lot of great engineers on the table.

So we start from the other end. We learn from founders what actually makes an engineer succeed on their team, then look for those qualities in people whose résumés may undersell them.

We're most interested in engineers who are better than their credentials suggest.  
  
**How to apply**

* Apply here or DM me on LinkedIn.
* We do want one answer: **What's the hardest or most interesting thing you've built, and what about it makes you think you're capable of more than your résumé shows?**

  + A few sentences is enough. A link to code or a project is even better. Specifics beat buzzwords.
  + If there's a fit, we'll talk, share what we know about each team, and help you figure out which roles make sense. When there's a strong match, we'll connect you directly with the founders.

**And if you've ever thought, "I'm a much better engineer than my résumé makes me look," we especially want to hear from you.**  
  
**One last thing**

Looking past credentials doesn't mean looking past ability.

If you're mass-applying without reading the post, can't show real engineering work, have a fabricated or misleading LinkedIn profile, or aren't authorized to work in the United States, please don't apply.

**It's not a good use of anyone's time.**

We'll overlook a pedigree. We won't overlook a lack of effort, skill, or honesty.  
  
**Show us what you've shipped, not what you say you can ship.**

Compensation Range: $150K - $350K
